subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: For stale PTY-backed background exec runs from a previous gateway epoch, should OpenClaw kill them on startup, reattach/re-register them, or land only in-process reconciliation first?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent behavior changes operator expectations for long-running background work after restart and needs maintainer policy intent before automation should implement it.

options.title: Kill stale previous-epoch runs
options.body: Persist active PTY metadata and sweep startup orphans with process-tree termination, treating reattach as a future explicit feature.

options.title: Reattach previous-epoch runs
options.body: Persist enough state to adopt live PTY trees after restart, accepting a larger state and session-correctness contract.

options.title: Land in-process mitigation only
options.body: Use the open PR to clean drift inside a live gateway while leaving cold-start orphan reaping as a known follow-up gap.

recommendation.title: Kill stale previous-epoch runs
recommendation.body: Persist active PTY metadata and sweep startup orphans with process-tree termination, treating reattach as a future explicit feature.

likelyOwner.reason: Background exec session behavior and timeout policy both have direct history from this owner path, making them a strong routing candidate for the policy choice.
